description:
**File**: `src/rate_limiter.cr`

**Severity**: P3 (architecture.md §2 "Single responsibility")

`RateLimiter.allowed?` does two unrelated things in one method:
1. Reads/writes the in-process `@@allowed_cache` (a Hash with TTL)
2. Calls `ThrottlerActor.instance.allowed` (delegates to actor)

The class-level state (`@@cache_mutex`, `@@allowed_cache`) leaks
through `cache_size` and `clear_cache`. Callers have to reason about
both layers even though they should be separable.

**Fix sketch**:
1. Extract `RateLimiterCache` module (Hash + TTL + cap)
2. Keep `RateLimiter` as a thin wrapper that consults the cache
   then falls through to the actor
3. Or: move the cache INSIDE ThrottlerActor (closer to its
   authoritative state)

Related: `quickhea-mcn` (cache to avoid per-request def_call) is
already closed. This ticket addresses the structure of the
wrapper, not the caching itself.

Found during code review 2026-06-18, see
`planning/code-review-2026-06-18.md` §3.1.
title: RateLimiter mixes cache + delegate in one class (single responsibility)
